caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 286 of 1995.
lawyer:
Syed Mahmudul Ahsan, Advocate (appeared with leave of the Court) instructed Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-record, Supreme Court — For the Petitioner. 
Not represented — For the Respondents.
parties:
Mukbul Ahmed Defendant No.1 ----- Petitioner.
vs.
Oliuddin Bhuiyan and others ----- Plaintiff-Respondents.
full_judgment: 4. Mr. Syed Mahmudul Ahsan, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, with the leave of the Court, submitted that the court below as well as the High Court Division erred in not holding that the suit for partition was not maintainable inasmuch as the plaintiff-respondents made a specific statement in the plaint that they had separated their share in the disputed property by mutating their names in separate Khatian No. 1751. The learned Advocate further submitted that Avilash, one of the sons of Brindaban, got the entire disputed plot No. 7875 by amicable partition amongst the brothers and on the death of Avilash his sons sold the land of said plot to defendant No.1. Hence there was no cause of action for instituting the present suit for partition.
